summary: Operation Red Eclipse is a single-player browser game (Unity 6, WebGL) where you design and fly a complete Mars science mission. You choose the launcher, satellite, instruments and orbit while a traffic-light system flags mass, power, cost and slot limits, and a computed reach uses the vis-viva and rocket equations. Then you run six months of operations: switch instruments on, mark regions of Gale Crater on a map of Mars, send data to Earth during contact windows and decide how to handle events such as dust storms. If no evidence has reached Earth by the end of month 6, Mission Control cancels the mission. The game makes the trade-offs of real mission design concrete for students. It is playable in English and Spanish.
details:
What it does: Operation Red Eclipse is a single-player game for the web browser (Unity 6, WebGL) in which the player designs and operates a complete Mars science mission, from the briefing to the final report. It is playable in English, with a Spanish option, and the radio transmissions are voiced in both languages.

How it works: (1) Briefing: Mission Control states the mission and the evidence the mission must bring back. (2) Configuration: the player chooses the launcher, satellite, instruments and orbit. A traffic-light system shows when mass, power, cost or slot limits are exceeded, and a computed reach accounts for real braking using the vis-viva equation and the rocket equation. (3) Tool loading: the player decides which extra equipment to carry. (4) Launch cinematic. (5) Monthly operations: switch instruments on, mark regions on a map of Mars (Gale Crater), resolve the month, send data to Earth when a contact window is open, and decide how to respond to events. If no evidence has reached Earth by the end of month 6, Mission Control cancels the mission. (6) Report: victory, partial success or failure, with a score.

Benefits and impact: every decision has a cost. Students who rarely get to experiment with a whole mission see how orbit, instruments, power, mass, budget and communications compete, and why real missions balance them.

Tools and technologies: Unity 6 (6000.6.9f1), C#, TextMeshPro, WebGL build of 57 MB, Python (Pillow) and Blender for asset processing, ffmpeg for audio, Git and GitHub. The project has 366 EditMode and 24 PlayMode automated tests, all passing. Fonts: Rajdhani, Barlow and IBM Plex Mono (SIL OFL). Icons: Lucide (ISC). The code and our own assets are MIT-licensed.

Creativity and factors considered: we scaled real instrument data (THEMIS, SHARAD, HiRISE, MCS and CRISM) into game values and used NASA 3D models as the look of the spacecraft. The player must always trade capability against mass, power and cost.

Super Intelligence (SI) use: code, tests and documents were written with Claude Code (Anthropic); music, sound effects and voices were generated with ElevenLabs. Design decisions and review were made by the team (Adrian and Diego). Details: IA.md in the repository.

Source code: https://github.com/Pholis07/OperacionEclipseRojo
